bug.description: Light theme, .delete-button in its :active (pressed) state has text contrast 4.46:1, below the 4.5:1 required by criterion 7 (text #b3122a on rgba(179,18,42,0.24) tint over white). Resting (white, 6.06+), hover (5.59) and busy (5.46) states pass. Dark theme pressed is 5.94, fine.
bug.reproduction: Light scheme, open http://127.0.0.1:PORT/, mouseMoved onto .delete-button then Input.dispatchMouseEvent mousePressed (do not release over the button); compute contrast of getComputedStyle(btn).color against button bg composited over the page: 4.46. Fix idea (not implemented by me): lower --danger-active alpha (e.g. 0.18) or darken --danger slightly.

verification.self_critique: Not tested: real Windows high-contrast/forced-colors mode (only the CSS rule's existence was seen), real touch devices (touch emulation only), browsers other than Chrome 1xx headless, :has() fallback. The hover:none check used touch emulation because setEmulatedMedia does not support those features. Contrast was computed by my own in-page compositing (sRGB WCAG formula), not a library, and backdrop-filter blur of the header was ignored. Pressed-state contrast was sampled 30ms after mousePressed; a subpixel difference from antialiasing is not a factor but the 4.46 value is very close to the threshold. Hovering a disabled busy button still applies the hover background (cosmetic, not a spec violation). Contrast of text on photos and the pseudo-element glyph colors beyond ::before were not separately sampled. The index.html "unchanged" claim relies on mtime and content because there is no git history.
